evals.name: reads-topic-docs-state-before-interview
evals.expected_output: Reads .claude/topic-docs.yaml first when present and reports effective values, applying documented defaults to absent keys. With no concern file it inspects project instructions and conforming layouts before asking one recommendation-first question covering every schema key.
expectations: Reads an existing .claude/topic-docs.yaml before proposing changes
Treats project instructions as an inference source rather than a competing runtime authority
Recommends the documented contract and memory tier defaults when no convention exists
Offers and preserves every topic-docs schema key

evals.name: fails-closed-on-ignored-contract-tier
evals.prompt:
/verification:setup

Use contract_tier: branch and contract_dir: docs/topics. The repository ignores docs/topics/**.
evals.expected_output: Runs git check-ignore -v against a representative file path such as docs/topics/probe/PLAN.md before writing. When an ignore rule matches, it stops, reports the exact matching rule and source line, and does not create or update .claude/topic-docs.yaml.
expectations: Checks a representative contract file path rather than only the directory
Stops before persistence when the branch-tier contract root is ignored
Reports the matching ignore rule and source
Never edits an ignore file to force the configuration through

evals.name: persists-tracked-concern-file-idempotently
evals.prompt:
/verification:setup

Accept the recommended defaults and preserve an existing vault_backend: docs key.
evals.expected_output: Writes a schema-valid tracked .claude/topic-docs.yaml without dropping the existing vault_backend key, verifies or creates the resolved memory root's self-ignoring .gitignore with an announcement, and reports the effective values. An immediate re-run reads the same state and does not rewrite equivalent values.
expectations: Persists configuration only in the tracked .claude/topic-docs.yaml concern file
Produces a schema-valid object rather than a comment-only YAML document
Preserves all existing schema keys on reconfiguration
Verifies the resolved memory root self-ignore and announces any creation
Re-running does not rewrite an equivalent configuration
